items.title: Second Public Hearing: Neighborhood Schools Attendance Boundary Change Study

publicComments.name: Matt Collier
publicComments.summary: Requested that the board restore both sides of Alameda de las Pulgas to the Roy Cloud boundary in Scenario 3, as the change would split his children between two different schools.

publicComments.name: William Paxton
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for Scenario 3, particularly for keeping the Kentwood/Atherwood neighborhood assigned to Henry Ford School given the lack of pedestrian access to Garfield.

publicComments.name: Anna Fonseca Janoff
publicComments.summary: Asked whether the redistricting goal was to move away from neighborhood schools to larger comprehensive campuses, and questioned how Scenarios 1 and 3 would improve socioeconomic diversity at Roy Cloud compared to Scenario 2.

publicComments.name: Michael Bergeron
publicComments.summary: Representing the Woodside Hills HOA, requested that Woodside Hills be reassigned to Roy Cloud (K–8) to encourage families currently in private schools to return to public school and build community.

publicComments.name: Brian Varese
publicComments.summary: Leaned toward Scenario 2 as better for long-term balance and diversity, questioned whether the school-of-choice lottery is truly promoting diversity by design, and asked that whichever scenario is chosen address schools pushed to 80% or above capacity.

publicComments.name: Selena Holder
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2, arguing that changing Roy Cloud's boundaries would encourage Selby Lane neighborhood families currently in private schools to return to public school and improve diversity.

publicComments.name: Keely Vega
publicComments.summary: Strongly supported Scenario 2 for long-term district balance, challenged the notion that school-of-choice seats promote intentional diversity, questioned the use of walkability as a boundary criterion, and asked how the board plans to weigh the survey showing 88% support for Scenario 2.

publicComments.name: Patricia Boers
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 to foster community among Woodside Hills children, noted her family's ethnic diversity and Spanish-speaking home as factors relevant to the diversity discussion, and pointed out that only about 30 students from Woodside Hills would be affected.

publicComments.name: Colleen Voss
publicComments.summary: Co-signer of the Selby Lane community letter supporting Scenario 2, argued it was unfair that the community-input Scenario 3 resembles Scenario 1 rather than the survey-preferred Scenario 2, and asked why Scenario 2 wasn't also refined with minor tweaks.

publicComments.name: Frank Hanig
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 or a minor tweak to Scenario 3 to include Woodside Hills in Roy Cloud, citing Fernside and Alameda as geographic barriers to Henry Ford and noting it would allow walkable K–8 attendance without significantly raising Roy Cloud's capacity percentage.

publicComments.name: David Eicher
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 to move Woodside Hills from Henry Ford/Kennedy to Roy Cloud, emphasizing the K–8 continuity that would help build community bonds and might bring private-school families back to public school.

publicComments.name: Lindsay Semple
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 or a Scenario 3 tweak assigning Woodside Hills to Roy Cloud, stating it would help build sub-community and move families away from private school or school-of-choice options.

publicComments.name: Abraham Fraley
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 for the Selby Lane area, citing dangerous crossing conditions on the state highway to Henry Ford, argued for boundary/demographic alignment with the Roy Cloud census area, and raised concerns about inherent bias when school-of-choice is prioritized over rezoned neighborhood students.

publicComments.name: Lisa Carr
publicComments.summary: Longtime Redwood City public school supporter living in Woodside Hills urged the board to listen to the strong community support for Scenario 2 or a Scenario 3 tweak including Woodside Hills in Roy Cloud, noting that neighborhood children are not currently attending public school.

publicComments.name: Katha Hall
publicComments.summary: Woodside Hills resident of 23 years supported having the neighborhood assigned to Roy Cloud to build community and bring children out of private schools, citing the 88% survey support for Scenario 2 as deserving respect.

items.title: Consent Items (Action Required) — as amended (10.1 pulled)
Approval of Measure U Application for 2020-21, Connect Community Charter School (PULLED)
Action Items
Adoption of Roadmap to Reopening / School Plan

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: Asked for specific hours of live Mandarin-immersion instruction per day and cautioned against encouraging small-group playdates as a safety risk.

publicComments.name: Brian Cagle
publicComments.summary: Advocated for continuing PE instruction during distance learning and cautioned that outdoor learning would frequently be uncomfortably hot, cold, or wet.

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: Asked for testing and contact-tracing protocols before return to campus, requested teachers be given the option to teach from home or classroom, and recommended waiting at least 14 days after holiday breaks before any in-person reopening.

publicComments.name: Michelle Torit
publicComments.summary: Supported the distance-learning decision and recommended postponing any school reopening until at least 14 days after winter break (January 19) to reduce exposure from holiday gatherings.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: Stressed that timely testing, tracking, and tracing protocols must be in place before any return to campus, and expressed hope to meet her TK students in person this year.

publicComments.name: Jamie Guiena
publicComments.summary: Echoed support for keeping PE in the daily distance-learning curriculum to address students' physical, social, and mental health needs during sedentary remote schooling.

publicComments.name: Julia Feng
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for including special-needs students in planning and asked what tools and strategies could help parents support very young learners who struggle or refuse to engage with screen-based learning.

publicComments.name: Kayla Kamley
publicComments.summary: As a first-grade teacher, urged the district to distribute technology and hotspots early, provide physical books and school supplies to students, and communicate class assignments and daily schedules to families well before the school year begins.

publicComments.name: Sarah La Torre
publicComments.summary: Proposed that the GATE program adopt a materials-pickup-plus-virtual-class model similar to the public library's art program to provide enrichment and a sense of normalcy during distance learning.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Asked when child care options would be announced and which highest-need students would be prioritized, requested home supply kits for students, and urged that technology be distributed before the start of school to avoid loss of instructional time.

publicComments.name: Teresita Carlos
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board and staff, shared that she is keeping her own preschool child home to avoid exposure, praised a Henry Ford teacher for excellent distance-learning that combined online and paper-based activities, and supported waiting until after winter break to consider returning.
